ownership_decision.invariant: Identity only resolves the authenticated Session's Workspace scope and does not own Activity or lifecycle facts. Run, Creation, Packaging and Publishing each own their source facts; the HTTP composition layer may merge but never reinterpret those facts.

boundary_decision.interaction: Each lifecycle owner exposes a narrow Workspace-scoped Activity facts reader. The HTTP composition layer receives those readers through apiserver.NewApp, queries them with the Session-derived Workspace, merges their already-classified facts, applies the public cursor, and maps them to the OpenAPI response without importing owner packages into one another.
boundary_decision.consistency: Synchronous live reads; pagination is stable for an unchanged dataset and does not claim a cross-request snapshot. If any enabled source is unavailable, the endpoint fails closed with HTTP 503, complete=false and unavailable_sources, returning neither items nor a cursor.
prohibited_dependencies: cross-context SQL or generated query row sharing
one lifecycle context importing another to build Activity
analytics events used as domain truth
silent omission of an unavailable source

domain_forces: Activity must help a returning creator decide what to do next without becoming a second state machine or hiding the exact source object.
Run, Creation, Packaging and Publishing use different state machines and timestamp semantics, so a generic handler cannot safely infer actionability or recency from raw status strings.
A useful cross-source feed must degrade visibly when a source fails and must paginate the union rather than paginate each existing list independently.
The current Run-only UI is honest and should remain the visible scope until every contracted owner source is implemented.
implementation_design.decision: Use no new Aggregate, event stream or persisted Activity context. Each owner provides a minimal read DTO containing its own classification, original status, authoritative last_updated_at, stable source identity and typed continuation target. GET /me/activity uses an opaque cursor ordered by group_rank, last_updated_at descending, kind and source_id; the live feed promises stable continuation only while the underlying dataset is unchanged. The API composition layer performs only Workspace-scoped fan-in, deterministic keyset merge, source-coverage reporting and transport mapping. Apply Jesse James Garrett's five planes in order: the return-and-resume outcome fixes Strategy; the four long-work sources and exclusions fix Scope; owner facts and composition fix Structure; grouping, ordering and one continuation action fix Skeleton; the existing design system fixes Surface.
invariants_preserved: Workspace scope comes from the authenticated Session and is applied by every owner reader.
Each lifecycle context remains authoritative for its statuses, transitions and actionable meaning.
Activity remains a read projection and never changes or repairs source state.
Run execution success, evaluation outcome, package status, publication status and Catalog exposure remain distinct facts.
Unknown, unavailable and empty remain distinguishable in both API and UI.
rejected_alternatives: A new persisted Activity context: current evidence requires a query projection, not another state source with replay and consistency obligations.
Identity owning lifecycle classification: Identity may resolve Workspace scope but must not absorb Run, Creation, Packaging or Publishing rules.
Browser-side composition: it cannot provide one authorization boundary, global cursor or truthful source coverage.
Entrypoint status mapping: it would move product rules into the composition root and break when an owner adds a state.
A single cross-context SQL query: it bypasses owner Services and hard-codes unrelated schemas into one read path.
Analytics-backed Activity: measurement data is intentionally not a second source of domain truth.

contract_change.description: Add GET /me/activity as a Session-authenticated Workspace Activity endpoint with a discriminated item union, deterministic keyset cursor and explicit source coverage. Existing lifecycle list endpoints and the compatible /workspace/runs UI route remain unchanged during migration.
contract_change.compatibility: Additive. Unknown item kinds and owner statuses remain displayable through stable summary fields; clients must not infer actionability from raw status.
contract_change.data_classification: Workspace-scoped metadata only; excludes full snapshots, prompts, trace payloads, evaluation text, package contents and review findings.
contract_change.retry_behavior: Read-only and idempotent. Any enabled owner read failure returns HTTP 503 with complete=false and unavailable_sources, without items or next_cursor; the client retries the whole read and never presents the failure as a complete empty Activity.

open_questions: Which owner states map to requires_action, in_progress and recent, and which continuation target is valid for each state?
Does Run Activity recency include cancellation requests and cleanup changes, or only Run lifecycle transitions?
Should Publishing project one Publication with its latest Release, and should Bundle Publication ship in the same first scope?
Which stable deep links select one Packaging Artifact and one Publication in the existing management spaces?
superseded_reason: Repository evidence now shows exact Artifact and Skill Publication continuations, Packaging quarantined is not a normal observable long-running phase, and the first source scope must exclude Bundle and Catalog exposure until their own contracts exist.
